item.title: Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code (CVE-2023-4863), bypass authentication (CVE-2026-16436 and CVE-2026-16437), or perform arbitrary operations (CVE-2026-16438), resulting in information disclosure, tampering with, destruction, or deletion of information, and a denial-of-service (DoS) condition of the system.

The following versions of Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz are affected:

  • Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS64 >=10.97|<=10.97.2 (CVE-2023-4863)
  • Mitsubishi Electric ICONICS Suite >=10.97|<=10.97.2 (CVE-2023-4863)
  • Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS <=11.03 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437)
  • Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS64 <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric ICONICS Suite <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric Hyper Historian <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric AnalytiX <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric MobileHMI <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric IoTWorX <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437)
  • Mitsubishi Electric MC Works64 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS32 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437)
  • Mitsubishi Electric BizViz vers:all/* (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 9.1 Mitsubishi Electric Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS64
3 Vulnerabilities
Out-of-bounds Write, Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password, Incorrect Privilege Assignment

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: United States

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2023-4863
Out-of-bounds Write (CWE-787) vulnerability caused by libwebp, an internal component in GENESIS64 and ICONICS Suite could allow an authenticated local attacker to cause a heap-based buffer overflow and execute arbitrary code by importing a crafted file as an administrator for the affected product. As a result, the attacker may disclose internal information, tamper with, destroy, or delete internal information, or cause the affected system to enter a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
Read More

4 Affected Products

Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS64: >=10.97|<=10.97.2

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Mitsubishi Electric is releasing fixed version 10.97.3 or later for GENESIS64 and ICONICS Suite. Please download the fixed version from the link below and install it: "https://iconicsinc.my.site.com/community/s/resource-center/product-downloads". (Note: GENESIS64 is included in the ICONICS Suite installation.) For more information on the fixed version, please refer to the Mitsubishi Electric security advisory at "https://www.mitsubishielectric.com/psirt/vulnerability/pdf/2026-006_en.pdf".

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend configuring the PCs with the affected product installed so that only an administrator can log in, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend using the PCs with the affected product installed in the LAN and blocking remote login from untrusted networks and hosts, and from non-administrator users, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend blocking unauthorized access by using a firewall, virtual private network (VPN), etc. and allowing remote login only to administrator when internet access is required, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend restricting physical access to the PC with the affected product installed and the network to which the PC is connected, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend preventing the user from clicking on web links in emails from untrusted sources, or from opening attachments in untrusted emails, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend installing anti-virus software on the PC with the affected product installed, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-16436
Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password (CWE-640) vulnerability in GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32, and BizViz could allow a remote attacker to unlock the system by obtaining the challenge response by some means. The challenge response used to unlock the system is common to all users and fixed. As a result, the attacker may disclose, tamper with, destroy, or delete internal information, or cause the affected system to enter a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend configuring the PCs with the affected product installed so that only an administrator can log in, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend using the PCs with the affected product installed in the LAN and blocking remote login from untrusted networks and hosts, and from non-administrator users, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend restricting physical access to the PC with the affected product installed and the network to which the PC is connected, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend preventing the user from clicking on web links in emails from untrusted sources, or from opening attachments in untrusted emails, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend installing anti-virus software on the PC with the affected product installed, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend performing the following steps for GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and MC Works64, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability. (1) Delete the .dat file at the location specified below. This file name and location is different depending on the product version. (Version 10: C:\Program Files\ICONICS\GENESIS64\Components\ClientChallengeTable.dat; Version 11: C:\ProgramData\ICONICS\11\SecurityChallenges.dat) (2) Create a blank file with the same name and location. (3) Restrict the file system write and delete access to this file to a unique administrator account, different than the GENESIS administrator account.

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-16437
Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password (CWE-640) vulnerability in GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32, and BizViz could allow an authenticated local user with administrative privileges to unlock the system by tampering with the management file that stores the challenge response. Administrators are able to read and write the management file. But the management file is protected by Windows. As a result, the attacker may disclose, tamper with, destroy, or delete internal information, or cause the affected system to enter a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

CVE-2026-16438
Incorrect Privilege Assignment (CWE-266) vulnerability in GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, and MC Works64 could allow an attacker who can log in using the same administrator account for the affected products to launch and operate DCOM objects locally or remotely. During installation, the installers of the affected products unnecessarily grant default DCOM permissions to the administrator account of the affected products. As a result, the attacker may disclose, tamper with, destroy, or delete internal information, or cause the affected system to enter a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Mitsubishi Electric is releasing fixed version 10.98 or later for GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, and MobileHMI. Please download the fixed version from the link below and install it: "https://iconicsinc.my.site.com/community/s/resource-center/product-downloads". (Note: GENESIS64, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, and MobileHMI are included in the ICONICS Suite installation.) For more information on the fixed version, please refer to the Mitsubishi Electric security advisory at "https://www.mitsubishielectric.com/psirt/vulnerability/pdf/2026-006_en.pdf".

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend configuring the PCs with the affected product installed so that only an administrator can log in, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend using the PCs with the affected product installed in the LAN and blocking remote login from untrusted networks and hosts, and from non-administrator users, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend blocking unauthorized access by using a firewall, virtual private network (VPN), etc. and allowing remote login only to administrator when internet access is required, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend restricting physical access to the PC with the affected product installed and the network to which the PC is connected, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend preventing the user from clicking on web links in emails from untrusted sources, or from opening attachments in untrusted emails, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend using the PCs with the affected product installed in the LAN and blocking access from untrusted networks and hosts through firewalls, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend blocking unauthorized access by using a firewall, virtual private network (VPN), etc. when internet access is required, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend installing anti-virus software on the PC with the affected product installed, as well as on any PCs that can access it, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

Summary

Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to cause a denial-of-service condition, corrupt memory, disclose sensitive information, or potentially execute arbitrary code.

The following versions of EPICS Base are affected:

  • EPICS Base release <=7.0.10 (CVE-2026-114595, CVE-2026-114596, CVE-2026-114597, CVE-2026-114598)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 9.8 The EPICS Community EPICS Base release
3 Vulnerabilities
Integer Overflow or Wraparound, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Global

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-114595
In EPICS Base release 7.0.10 and prior, an integer overflow in network request processing can cause memory to be allocated with an incorrect size. Subsequent handling of attacker supplied data may result in memory corruption, denial of service, or potential remote code execution.
Read More

1 Affected Product

The EPICS Community EPICS Base release: <=7.0.10

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
The EPICS Community has made available updates to the epics-base GitHub repositories. Affected users should update to the 7.0.11 release. For more information, users should contact the EPICS Controls team https://epics-controls.org/support/.

item.title: Siemens Software Center
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

The affected application loads dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) from an uncontrolled search path. This could allow an authenticated local attacker to place a specially crafted DLL in a directory that the application searches, leading to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the affected application. Siemens has released a new version for Siemens Software Center and recommends to update to the latest version. Please refer to our blog post for additional information about current known active exploitation and how to detect it.

The following versions of Siemens Software Center are affected:

  • Siemens Software Center vers:intdot/<4.0.9.8 (CVE-2026-110936)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 6.7 Siemens Siemens Software Center
1 Vulnerability
Uncontrolled Search Path Element

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-110936
The affected application loads dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) from an uncontrolled search path. This could allow an authenticated local attacker to place a specially crafted DLL in a directory that the application searches, leading to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the affected application.
Read More

1 Affected Product

Siemens Software Center < V4.0.9.8

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Update to V4.0.9.8 or later version (All existing versions of SSC will be auto updated on next startup. The latest version can also be downloaded in the respective link)

Additional Metrics

General Recommendations

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

item.description:

Summary

Successful exploitation of this these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to fully compromise the device.

The following versions of Kiloview E3 NDI Encoder are affected:

  • E3 Firmware <1.30 (CVE-2026-109122, CVE-2026-111100, CVE-2026-96616, CVE-2026-105265, CVE-2026-110491, CVE-2026-107861, CVE-2026-110243, CVE-2026-92450, CVE-2026-110825)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 9.9 Kiloview E3 Firmware
6 Vulnerabilities
Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection'), Missing Authentication for Critical Function, Insufficient Session Expiration, Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'), NULL Pointer Dereference, Use of Hard-coded Credentials

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Communications, Information Technology
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: China

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-109122
The network management service on affected Kiloview E3 NDI encoder firmware fails to sanitize one field used when configuring static routes via the web management API. An authenticated web user with permission to configure static routes can exploit this to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root, and the malicious configuration persists across reboots. Successful exploitation could result in full device compromise, including exposure of stored credentials and cryptographic material.

item.title: Siemens Industrial Edge App Publisher
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

The Industrial Edge App Publisher contains a vulnerability chain involving improper certificate validation and the rendering of unescaped data from backend responses. These issues can be combined to allow an attacker on the network to impersonate the management server and execute arbitrary code (RCE) on the local machine through Node.js integration. Siemens has released an update for the Industrial Edge App Publisher and recommends to update to the latest version.

The following versions of Siemens Industrial Edge App Publisher are affected:

  • Industrial Edge App Publisher vers:intdot/<1.27.9 (CVE-2026-78556, CVE-2026-78557)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 8.3 Siemens Industrial Edge App Publisher
2 Vulnerabilities
Improper Certificate Validation, Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-78556
The affected software does not properly validate the server certificate when initiating a TLS connection. This allows an attacker to intercept and relay communication (Man-in-the-Middle attack) and to spoof a trusted entity by interfering in the communication path between the client and the intended server.
Read More

1 Affected Product

Industrial Edge App Publisher < V1.27.9

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Update to V1.27.9 or later version

Additional Metrics

Relevant CWE: CWE-295 Improper Certificate Validation

CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String
3.1 7.4 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-78557
The application fails to properly sanitize or escape data received from the backend before rendering it in the user interface. Because the front end is integrated with Node.js, this vulnerability allows for the execution of arbitrary JavaScript, which can be leveraged to achieve remote code execution (RCE) on the victim's machine
Read More

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity

Recommended Practices

item.description:

Summary

PSS(R)SINCAL uses WibuKey third-party product that contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to cause a system crash, resulting in a denial-of-service condition. This affects PSS SINCAL only when configured to use the legacy WibuKey dongle license type. Siemens is actively preparing updates and recommends applicable mitigations for products where patches are currently unavailable.

The following versions of Siemens PSS(R)SINCAL are affected:

  • PSS(R)SINCAL V21.5 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-84854)
  • PSS(R)SINCAL V22.0 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-84854)
  • PSS(R)SINCAL V22.5 vers:intdot/<22.5.5 (CVE-2026-84854)

In the WibuKey driver, insufficient validation of user input when calculating the size of a kernel buffer could cause small amounts of data to be written outside the intended kernel buffer. This can lead to a system crash. Under unfavorable circumstances, adjacent kernel memory may be modified.

Operators of critical power systems (e.g. TSOs or DSOs) worldwide are usually required by regulations to build resilience into the power grids by applying multi-level redundant secondary protection schemes. It is therefore recommended that the operators check whether appropriate resilient protection measures are in place. The risk of cyber incidents impacting the grid's reliability can thus be minimized by virtue of the grid design. Siemens strongly recommends applying the provided security updates using the corresponding tooling and documented procedures made available with the product. If supported by the product, an automated means to apply the security updates across multiple product instances may be used. Siemens strongly recommends prior validation of any security update before being applied, and supervision by trained staff of the update process in the target environment. As a general security measure Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access with appropriate mechanisms (e.g. firewalls, segmentation, VPN). It is advised to configure the environment according to our operational guidelines in order to run the devices in a protected IT environment.

item.title: Siemens SIMATIC IPCs
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

The products listed below contain a vulnerability that could allow an attacker to boot an operating system or UEFI application signed with that test key, bypassing UEFI Secure Boot protections even when Secure Boot is enabled. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.

The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC IPCs are affected:

  • SIMATIC IPC BX-21A vers:intdot/<31.01.13 (CVE-2026-72895)
  • SIMATIC IPC RW-543A vers:intdot/<1.1.4 (CVE-2026-72895)
  • SIMATIC IPC227G / IPC277G / IPC277G PRO / IPC327G / IPC377G vers:intdot/<28.01.15 (CVE-2026-72895)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 7.7 Siemens SIMATIC IPC BX-21A
1 Vulnerability
Use of Default Cryptographic Key

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-72895
A BIOS vendor test key is present in the UEFI Secure Boot key database. This could allow a local attacker with physical or administrative access to the device to boot an operating system or UEFI application signed with that test key, bypassing UEFI Secure Boot protections even when Secure Boot is enabled, potentially leading to a full loss of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the device.
Read More

3 Affected Products

SIMATIC IPC BX-21A < V31.01.13

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation

Note: After upgrading to the fixed BIOS version, users must load the BIOS default settings. If Secure Boot keys were already provisioned, they must be provisioned again afterwards.

Mitigation
As a temporary mitigation, users can manually remove the test key from the database (e.g., "DO NOT TRUST - AMI Test PK" for RW-543A or "insyde-ElkhartLake" for IPC227G/277G/327G/377G and BX-21A). Note: Loading default settings will restore the test key, so upgrading remains recommended.

Vendor fix
Update to V31.01.13 or later version

SIMATIC IPC RW-543A < V1.1.4

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation

Note: After upgrading to the fixed BIOS version, users must load the BIOS default settings. If Secure Boot keys were already provisioned, they must be provisioned again afterwards.

Mitigation
As a temporary mitigation, users can manually remove the test key from the database (e.g., "DO NOT TRUST - AMI Test PK" for RW-543A or "insyde-ElkhartLake" for IPC227G/277G/327G/377G and BX-21A). Note: Loading default settings will restore the test key, so upgrading remains recommended.

Vendor fix
Update to V1.1.4 or later version

SIMATIC IPC227G / IPC277G / IPC277G PRO / IPC327G / IPC377G < V28.01.15

Remediations

Mitigation

Note: After upgrading to the fixed BIOS version, users must load the BIOS default settings. If Secure Boot keys were already provisioned, they must be provisioned again afterwards.

As a temporary mitigation, users can manually remove the test key from the database (e.g., "DO NOT TRUST - AMI Test PK" for RW-543A or "insyde-ElkhartLake" for IPC227G/277G/327G/377G and BX-21A). Note: Loading default settings will restore the test key, so upgrading remains recommended.

Acknowledgments

  • Siemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.

General Recommendations

As a general security measure Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to affected products with appropriate mechanisms. It is advised to follow recommended security practices in order to run the devices in a protected IT environment.

Additional Resources

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

Terms of Use

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

Advisory Conversion Disclaimer

This ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-333035 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. Please contact Siemens ProductCERT directly for any questions regarding this advisory.

item.title: Siemens Industrial Edge Device Kit
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Users of Industrial Edge Devices are advised to consult the respective Security Advisories for their devices (for Siemens Industrial Edge devices see Additional Information). Industrial Edge Device Kit contains multiple path traversal vulnerabilities that could facilitate an authenticated remote attacker to access sensitive internal information. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens recommends specific countermeasures for products where fixes are not, or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens Industrial Edge Device Kit are affected:

  • Industrial Edge Device Kit - arm64 V1.10 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-44414, CVE-2026-44415)
  • Industrial Edge Device Kit - arm64 V1.11 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-44414, CVE-2026-44415)

View CVE Details

Acknowledgments

  • Siemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.

General Recommendations

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity

Additional Resources

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

Terms of Use

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

Advisory Conversion Disclaimer

This ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-377139 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. Please contact Siemens ProductCERT directly for any questions regarding this advisory.

item.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW contains multiple vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database, retrieve sensitive administrative credentials, escalate privileges, and perform unauthorized operations such as modifying system configurations or causing a denial of service. Siemens has released a new version for RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW and recommends to update to the latest version.

The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW are affected:

  • RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW vers:intdot/<6.0 (CVE-2026-89196, CVE-2026-89197, CVE-2026-89198, CVE-2026-89199, CVE-2026-89200, CVE-2026-89201, CVE-2026-89202, CVE-2026-89203, CVE-2026-89204, CVE-2026-89205, CVE-2026-89206)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 8.8 Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW
4 Vulnerabilities
Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection'), Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key, Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data, Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

Affected devices do not properly validate or sanitize input in facility names processed during the Bulk Import/Export workflow. This could allow an authenticated attacker with specific privileges to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the underlying database.

Summary

Multiple SIMATIC WinCC versions are affected by a database privilege escalation vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user with access to the database to execute commands on the underlying host system. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens is preparing further fixes and recommends mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens WinCC are affected:

  • SIMATIC WinCC V7.5 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-59241)
  • SIMATIC WinCC V8.0 vers:intdot/<8.0.0.11 (CVE-2026-59241)

item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) contains multiple vulnerabilities in the integrated SQLite component that could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code, cause a denial of service, or obtain sensitive information. Siemens has released a new version for RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) and recommends to update to the latest version.

The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller are affected:

  • RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) vers:intdot/<6.0 (CVE-2025-6965, CVE-2025-70873, CVE-2025-71316, CVE-2026-11822, CVE-2026-11824)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 9.8 Siemens RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC)
4 Vulnerabilities
Numeric Truncation Error, Improper Clearing of Heap Memory Before Release ('Heap Inspection'), Improper Handling of Unicode Encoding, Heap-based Buffer Overflow

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2025-6965
There exists a vulnerability in SQLite versions before 3.50.2 where the number of aggregate terms could exceed the number of columns available. This could lead to a memory corruption issue. We recommend upgrading to version 3.50.2 or above.
Read More

1 Affected Product

RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0

Product Status: known_affected

View CVE Details

CVE-2025-70873
An information disclosure issue in the zipfileInflate function in the zipfile extension in SQLite v3.51.1 and earlier allows attackers to obtain heap memory via supplying a crafted ZIP file.
Read More

RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW Station Access Controller (SAC) < V6.0

View CVE Details

CVE-2025-71316
SQLite 'sqldiff.exe' does not securely handle the way the Microsoft Windows C runtime converts Unicode characters to ANSI codepages. An attacker could use the '-L' option to load an arbitrary DLL with a crafted command line argument string that results in command line file arguments being misinterpreted as command line options. Fixed on or around 2025-12-26.

3.1 9.8 CRITICAL CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-11822
SQLite before 3.53.2 contains memory corruption vulnerabilities in the FTS5 full-text search extension that allow attackers to cause process crashes, memory exhaustion, or arbitrary code execution by supplying a crafted database with malformed FTS5 page data. Attackers can trigger an out-of-bounds read in fts5LeafSeek() via an attacker-controlled loop bound and a heap buffer overflow write in fts5ChunkIterate() through a crafted continuation page causing an integer underflow, exploitable when an FTS5 MATCH query is executed against the malicious database.

CVE-2026-11824
SQLite before 3.53.2 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the FTS5 full-text search extension that allows attackers to cause a crash or execute arbitrary code by supplying a crafted database with malicious continuation page metadata specifying a szLeaf value smaller than 4. Attackers can trigger an integer underflow in fts5ChunkIterate() causing an inflated remaining byte count during FTS5 MATCH query processing, leading to a heap buffer overflow of attacker-controlled data in applications compiled with SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5.

Acknowledgments

  • Siemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.

General Recommendations

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity

Additional Resources

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

Terms of Use

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

Advisory Conversion Disclaimer

This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. item.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 Devices
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Nozomi Networks has published information on vulnerabilities in Nozomi Guardian/CMC. This advisory lists the related Siemens Industrial products affected by these vulnerabilities. Siemens recommends to contact customer support to receive patch and update information.

The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 Devices are affected:

  • RUGGEDCOM APE1808 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-33387, CVE-2026-33388, CVE-2026-33389, CVE-2026-33391, CVE-2026-33920)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 7.5 Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808
4 Vulnerabilities
Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine, Incorrect Authorization, Lack of Administrator Control over Security, Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-33387
A template injection vulnerability was discovered in the Dashboards functionality due to improper validation of an input parameter. An authenticated user with the required privileges can define a dashboard containing a malicious payload, or a victim can be socially engineered into importing a malicious dashboard. When the victim views or imports the dashboard, the payload executes in their browser context, allowing the attacker to modify application data or disrupt application availability.
Read More

1 Affected Product

RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMC

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Contact customer support to receive patch and update information

Additional Metrics

Relevant CWE: CWE-1336 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

CVE-2026-33388
An access control vulnerability was discovered in the Credentials Manager functionality due to insufficient validation of user privileges. A remote authenticated user with limited privileges can view a limited subset of the available entries in the Credentials Manager. The actual credential values are not directly visible, but the user can delete entries or edit their properties. An attacker who deletes or edits an entry can disrupt authentication for dependent devices, and one who manipulates an entry's configuration may be able to indirectly obtain the credentials.
Read More

RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Nozomi Guardian/CMC

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-33389
An improper certificate/host key validation vulnerability was discovered in the Smart Polling functionality, which established encrypted connections to target devices without validating the remote host's identity, and no option was provided to enable it. A man-in-the-middle attacker positioned between a sensor and a polled device can, during a polling session, impersonate the device and intercept the communication, including the credentials used to access it. The captured credentials can then be replayed to authenticate against the device itself or against other devices sharing the same credentials, allowing the attacker to access and tamper with the device's data and to disrupt its operations.

General Recommendations

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

item.title: Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Multiple vulnerabilities have been identified in the additional GNU/Linux subsystem of the SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP V1.1.1. Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP are affected:

  • SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP - GNU/Linux subsystem vers:all/* 
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 10 Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP - GNU/Linux subsystem
377 Vulnerabilities
Access of Uninitialized Pointer, Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow'), Deadlock, Detection of Error Condition Without Action, Double Free, Expired Pointer Dereference, Heap-based Buffer Overflow, Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection'), Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, Improper Handling of Missing Special Element, Improper Handling of Structural Elements, Improper Input Validation, Improper Locking, Improper Resource Locking, Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer, Improper Update of Reference Count, Improper Validation of Array Index, Improper Validation of Consistency within Input, Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input, Incorrect Synchronization, Integer Overflow or Wraparound, Integer Underflow (Wrap or Wraparound), Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop'), Missing Default Case in Multiple Condition Expression, Missing Initialization of Resource, Missing Lock Check, Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime, Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime, Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource, NULL Pointer Dereference, Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release, Out-of-bounds Read, Out-of-bounds Write, Plaintext Storage of a Password, Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference, Return of Wrong Status Code, Signal Handler Race Condition, Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition, Unchecked Return Value, Use After Free, Use of Incorrect Operator, Use of Uninitialized Resource, Write-what-where Condition

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2023-52927
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: netfilter: allow exp not to be removed in nf_ct_find_expectation Currently nf_conntrack_in() calling nf_ct_find_expectation() will remove the exp from the hash table. However, in some scenario, we expect the exp not to be removed when the created ct will not be confirmed, like in OVS and TC conntrack in the following patches. This patch allows exp not to be removed by setting IPS_CONFIRMED in the status of the tmpl.
Read More

1 Affected Product

SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP - GNU/Linux subsystem

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
Limit access to the interactive shell of the additional GNU/Linux subssytem to trusted personnel only.

Mitigation
Only build and run applications from trusted sources.

None available
Currently no fix is available

  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

item.title: Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Multiple vulnerabilities have been identified in the additional GNU/Linux subsystem of the firmware version V3.1.7 for the SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP (incl. SIPLUS variant). Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP are affected:

  • SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AB0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7
  • SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AC0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 
  • SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518F-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4FX00-1AB0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 
  • SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518F-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4FX00-1AC0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 
  • SIPLUS S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6AG1518-4AX00-4AC0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 10 Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AB0)
428 Vulnerabilities

('Classic Buffer Overflow'), Buffer Underwrite ('Buffer Underflow'), Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition'), Deadlock, Divide By Zero, Expired Pointer Dereference, Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies, Exposure of Sensitive Information in Shared Microarchitectural Structures during Transient Execution, Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow, Improper Following of Specification by Caller, Improper Handling of Invalid Use of Special Elements, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, Improper Handling of Missing Special Element, Improper Handling of Structural Elements, Improper Input Validation, Improper Locking, Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character, Improper Null Termination, Improper Privilege Management, Improper Resource Locking, Improper Resource Shutdown or Release, Improper Update of Reference Count, Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input, Improperly Implemented Security Check for Standard, Incomplete Cleanup, Incomplete Internal State Distinction, Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size, Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types, Incorrect Privilege Assignment, Incorrect Synchronization, Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast, Integer Overflow or Wraparound, Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop'), Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value, Misinterpretation of Input, Missing Critical Step in Authentication, Missing Default Case in Multiple Condition Expression, Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data, Missing Initialization of Resource, Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime, CVE-2021-41617
sshd in OpenSSH 6.2 through 8.x before 8.8, when certain non-default configurations are used, allows privilege escalation because supplemental groups are not initialized as expected. Acknowledgments

  • Siemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.

General Recommendations

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends protecting network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends configuring the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity

Additional Resources

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

Terms of Use

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the exploitation risk of this vulnerability.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most recent version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets. Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

item.title: Siemens SIMATIC S7 Webserver API
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

.NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API contains multiple vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information or write arbitrary files outside the intended download directory. Siemens has released a new version for .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API and recommends to update to the latest version.

The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7 Webserver API are affected:

  • .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API vers:intdot/<3.3.61, vers:intdot/<3.3.62 (CVE-2026-85114, CVE-2026-85115)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 7.5 Siemens .NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API
2 Vulnerabilities
Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'), Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-85114
Affected applications do not properly validate filenames received from remote servers during ticket downloads. This could allow an attacker who can manipulate the ticket response to write arbitrary files outside the intended download directory and, when overwriting is enabled, replace existing files accessible to the application.
Read More

1 Affected Product

.NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API < V3.3.61

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Update to V3.3.61 or later version

Additional Metrics

Relevant CWE: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String
3.1 7.5 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-85115
Affected applications do not properly redact PLC restore passwords from HTTP error exception messages. This could allow an attacker with access to logs or other diagnostic output to obtain the plaintext restore password and potentially perform unauthorized operations on the PLC.
Read More

2 Affected Products

.NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API < V3.3.61

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations
.NET Client Library for SIMATIC S7 Webserver API < V3.3.62

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Update to V3.3.62 or later version

Additional Metrics

Relevant CWE: CWE-209 Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String
3.1 5.5 MEDIUM CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

View CVE Details

Acknowledgments

  • Siemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.

General Recommendations

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity

Additional Resources

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

Terms of Use

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

Advisory Conversion Disclaimer

This ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-390352 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. Please contact Siemens ProductCERT directly for any questions regarding this advisory.

item.title: Moxa AIG-302 ThingsPro Edge
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to obtain and disclose sensitive information.

The following versions of Moxa AIG-302 ThingsPro Edge are affected:

  • Moxa AIG-302 ThingsPro Edge firmware <=1.4.0 (CVE-2026-109812, CVE-2026-109813)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 8.1 Moxa Moxa AIG-302 ThingsPro Edge firmware
2 Vulnerabilities
Missing Authorization, Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Water and Wastewater Systems
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Taiwan

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-109812
A missing authorization vulnerability exists in the internal API /api/v1/secrets/ for some of Moxa's industrial computing products. A privileged authenticated attacker with adjacent network access could exploit this vulnerability to access sensitive information, potentially resulting in the disclosure of confidential data, including cryptographic key material.
Read More

1 Affected Product

Moxa Moxa AIG-302 ThingsPro Edge firmware: <=1.4.0

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
Moxa has provided a fix for the vulnerability in v1.4.1. Users are encouraged to obtain and apply the update through one of the following methods:

Mitigation
If the AIG-302 has Internet access, login to the AIG-302 Web Console, go to Maintenance > Software Upgrades, and click Check for upgrades to check for and obtain the update.

Mitigation
Users can download the v1.4.1 patch manually from either the official AIG-302 product website or the Moxa Software Release Service. Then, log in to the AIG-302 Web Console, navigate to Maintenance > Software Upgrades, and select Package Upload to upload the patch.

Mitigation
Users can download the v1.4.1 patch manually from either the official AIG-302 product website or the Moxa Software Release Service. Then, log in to the AIG-302 Web Console, navigate to Maintenance > Software Upgrades, and select Package Upload to upload the patch.

Mitigation
For more information refer to Moxa's security advisory MPSA-262560

item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could crash the Windows kernel.

The following versions of HMS Networks PEAK-System PCAN Windows drivers are affected:

  • PEAK-System Device Driver Setup <=5.1.2.1151 (CVE-2026-109576, CVE-2026-101103, CVE-2026-94188, CVE-2026-103672, CVE-2026-110322, CVE-2026-105960)
  • PCAN Windows CAN device drivers <=5.1.2 (CVE-2026-109576, CVE-2026-101103, CVE-2026-94188, CVE-2026-103672, CVE-2026-110322, CVE-2026-105960)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 7.1 HMS Networks PEAK-System Device Driver Setup
5 Vulnerabilities
Out-of-bounds Write, Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow'), Improper Validation of Array Index, Untrusted Pointer Dereference, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Transportation Systems, Healthcare and Public Health, Energy, Critical Manufacturing
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Sweden

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-109576
The parser in PEAK-System PCAN driver correctly detected the malformed record, but the loop iterating the record list advanced its processed-bytes counter even when a record had been rejected as invalid.

HMS Networks PEAK-System Device Driver Setup: <=5.1.2.1151

Acknowledgments

  • Seyeon Bang reported these vulnerabilities to CISA.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as virtual private networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

CISA also recommends users take the following measures to protect themselves from social engineering attacks: Do not click web links or open attachments in unsolicited email messages. Refer to Recognizing and Avoiding Email Scams for more information on avoiding email scams. Refer to Avoiding Social Engineering and Phishing Attacks for more information on social engineering attacks.

No known public exploitation specifically targeting these vulnerabilities has been reported to CISA at this time. These vulnerabilities are not exploitable remotely.

Summary

Hitachi Energy is aware of vulnerabilities that affect RTU500 product versions listed in this document. These vulnerabilities if exploited can have impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of the product. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions for information about the mitigation/remediation.

The following versions of Hitachi Energy RTU500 Product are affected:

CVE-2026-17539
RTU500 has a vulnerability, where high-load scenarios, such as sending GI requests at short intervals, may cause a NULL pointer dereference in the last entry of the enhanced message queue. This can cause a BCI_IEC104 fatal write error, resulting in connection interruption and restart, and ultimately a denial of service for bidirectional IEC 60870-5-104 communication.

CVE-2026-28388
A vulnerability exists in OpenSSL library component of RTU500 that is used for secure HTTPS access, authenticating and establishing encrypted communications with other devices. When processing a malformed delta CRL with a Delta CRL Indicator but no required CRL Number extension, OpenSSL may dereference a NULL pointer, causing a Denial of Service during X.509 certificate verification. Exploitation requires delta CRL processing to be enabled, a relevant freshest CRL condition to be present, and an attacker-supplied malformed CRL. The issue is limited to Denial of Service and cannot lead to code execution or memory disclosure.

CVE-2026-11856
A vulnerability exists in the web-based management and services functions of RTU500 using libcurl library. When the same libcurl handle is reused after a transfer to one HTTP origin using Digest authentication, libcurl may incorrectly send the Authorization header intended for the first origin to a second origin. This can disclose authentication information to an unintended host.

Support

For additional information and support please contact your product provider or Hitachi Energy service organization. For contact information, see https://www.hitachienergy.com/contact-us/ for Hitachi Energy contact-centers.

General Mitigation Factors

Recommended security practices and firewall configurations can help protect a process control network from attacks that originate from outside the network. Such practices include that process control systems are physically protected from direct access by unauthorized personnel, have no direct connections to the Internet, and are separated from other networks by means of a firewall system that has a minimal number of ports exposed, and others that have to be evaluated case by case. Process control systems should not be used for Internet surfing, instant messaging, or receiving e-mails. Portable computers and removable storage media should be carefully scanned for viruses before they are connected to a control system. Proper password policies and processes should be followed. Additional information on Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices can be found in the Hitachi Energy “Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices” Cybersecurity Notification. [1]

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the exploitation risk of this vulnerability.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most recent version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets. Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

Summary

Hitachi Energy is aware of multiple vulnerabilities that affect MicroSCADA X SYS600 product versions listed in this document. These vulnerabilities can be exploited to carry out various attacks on the product. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions for information about the mitigation/remediation.

The following versions of Hitachi Energy MicroSCADA X SYS600 Product are affected:

  • MicroSCADA X SYS600 vers:MicroSCADA_X_SYS600/<=10.7, 10.8 (CVE-2026-9852, CVE-2026-9853, CVE-2026-9854, CVE-2026-9853)
CVSS Vendor Equipment

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Energy
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Switzerland

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-9852
A CSV injection vulnerability exists in SYS600. Injected malicious formulas can add or modify data to the spreadsheet, insert links, exfiltrate data, and in some cases, depending on how the user has their environment configured, execute malicious code on the user’s machine. To exploit this issue attackers would need a way to create arbitrary log messages. This could be achieved through normal functionality via SCIL scripts, a log injection vulnerability, or via the SYS600 broker. This vulnerability affects all Windows users regardless of their privilege level who can run the Notify service and export the log.
